title: Singular partitive of common -e words
summary: For the common -e words taught here, keep -e and add -tta/-ttä: perhe (“family”) → perhettä.
objectives: Form the singular partitive in this bounded word family.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: A case is a word form used for a grammatical job. The dictionary form is the form used to look up a word. The partitive has several uses; it does not always mean “some”. Here you practise forming the word, so no sentence construction is required.
For these e-ending words, add -tta/-ttä directly to the dictionary form. This spelling pattern produces a double t. Other e-ending families exist; practise only the listed family here.
keyPoints: Learn each word with its pattern; a similar final letter does not guarantee the same stem.

steps: perhe + ttä = perhettä; keep e and write double tt.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “family”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
huone + tta = huonetta; keep e and write double tt.

The word’s meaning stays connected to “address”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.

commonMistakes: Write double tt in these partitives.
Do not lengthen e before adding -tta/-ttä.
Choose the ending from the complete word’s vowels.
